page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, it features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 96 MB of L3 cache, with a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, has no local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test registers at 192014.4, placing it in the top 10% of tested hardware, while single-core performance remains in the average tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 13912.96 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 363.83 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 1131.71 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations reach 269.45 million operations per second.

Given its high core density and arm64 architecture, the instance offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that do not require x86 instruction sets. The lack of local storage and GPU hardware means it is optimized purely for CPU-bound tasks. It is highly suited for high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data compression, database operations, and medium-scale LLM inference prompt processing.
